cues.en: For hundreds of years, analog computers were the most powerful computers on earth predicting eclipses,
cues.zh: 数百年来，模拟计算机一直是地球上最强大的计算机，用来预测日食、

cues.en: tides, and guiding anti aircraft guns. Then with the advent of solid state transistors,
cues.zh: 潮汐，还能为高射炮提供瞄准指引。后来，随着固态晶体管问世，

cues.en: digital computers took off. Now virtually every computer we use is digital.
cues.zh: 数字计算机迅速崛起。如今，我们使用的几乎所有计算机都是数字式的。

cues.en: But today,
cues.zh: 但今天，

cues.en: a perfect storm of factors is setting the scene for a resurgence of analog technology.
cues.zh: 多种因素汇聚，正为模拟技术的复兴创造条件。

cues.en: This is an analog computer
cues.zh: 这是一台模拟计算机，

cues.en: and by connecting these wires in particular ways, I can program it to solve a whole range of differential equations.
cues.zh: 只要按特定方式连接这些导线，我就能编程让它求解一系列微分方程。

cues.en: For example, this setup allows me to simulate a damped mass oscillating on a spring. So on the oscilloscope, you can actually see the position of the mass over time,
cues.zh: 比如，这种接法可以模拟一个在弹簧上振荡的阻尼质量块。在示波器上，你能直接看到质量块的位置随时间的变化，

cues.en: and I can vary the damping
cues.zh: 我还可以改变阻尼，

cues.en: or the spring constant
cues.zh: 或弹簧常数，

cues.en: or the mass, and we can see how the amplitude and duration of the oscillations change.
cues.zh: 也可以改变质量，看看振荡的振幅和持续时间会如何变化。

cues.en: Now, what makes this an analog computer is that there are no zeros and ones in here. Instead, there's actually a voltage that oscillates up and down exactly like a mass on a spring. The electrical circuitry is an analog for the physical problem. It just takes place much faster.
cues.zh: 这台计算机之所以是模拟计算机，是因为里面没有 0 和 1。相反，电压会像弹簧上的质量块一样上下振荡。电路模拟了这个物理问题，只是运行得快得多。

cues.en: Now, if I change the electrical connections, I can program this computer to solve other differential equations like the Lorentz system, which is a basic model of convection in the atmosphere.
cues.zh: 现在，只要改变电路连接，我就能编程让这台计算机求解其他微分方程，比如描述大气对流的基本模型——Lorentz 系统。

cues.en: Now the Lorentz system is famous because it was one of the first discovered examples of chaos.
cues.zh: Lorentz 系统之所以著名，是因为它是最早被发现的混沌实例之一。

cues.en: And here, you can see the Lorentz attractor with its beautiful butterfly shape.
cues.zh: 在这里，你可以看到 Lorentz 吸引子，以及它美丽的蝴蝶形状。

cues.en: And on this analog computer, I can change the parameters
cues.zh: 在这台模拟计算机上，我可以改变参数

cues.en: and see their effects in real time.
cues.zh: 并实时看到它们的影响。

cues.en: So these examples illustrate some of the advantages of analog computers.
cues.zh: 所以这些例子说明了模拟计算机的一些优势。

cues.en: They are incredibly powerful computing devices and they can complete a lot of computations fast.
cues.zh: 它们是极其强大的计算设备，能快速完成大量计算。

cues.en: Plus, they don't take much power to do it.
cues.zh: 而且，做这些并不怎么耗电。

cues.en: With a digital computer, if you want to add two eight bit numbers, you need around 50 transistors.
cues.zh: 用数字计算机，要把两个 8 位数相加，大约需要 50 个晶体管。

cues.en: Whereas with an analog computer, you can add two currents
cues.zh: 而用模拟计算机，你可以把两股电流相加

cues.en: just by connecting
cues.zh: 只需连接

cues.en: two wires.
cues.zh: 两根导线。

cues.en: With a digital computer to multiply two numbers, you need on the order of a thousand transistors,
cues.zh: 用数字计算机把两个数相乘，需要大约一千个晶体管，

cues.en: all switching zeros and ones. Whereas with an analog computer, you can pass a current
cues.zh: 全都在切换 0 和 1。而用模拟计算机，你可以让一股电流

cues.en: through a resistor,
cues.zh: 通过一个电阻器，

cues.en: and then the voltage across this resistor
cues.zh: 然后这个电阻两端的电压

cues.en: will be I times r.
cues.zh: 就是 I 乘以 r。

cues.en: So effectively,
cues.zh: 所以实际上，

cues.en: you have multiplied
cues.zh: 你已经把

cues.en: two numbers together.
cues.zh: 两个数相乘了。

cues.en: But analog computers also have their drawbacks.
cues.zh: 但模拟计算机也有它们的缺点。

cues.en: For one thing, they are not general purpose computing devices. I mean, you're not gonna run Microsoft Word on this thing. And also, since the inputs and outputs are continuous,
cues.zh: 首先，它们不是通用计算设备。我是说，你不会在这东西上运行 Microsoft Word。而且，由于输入和输出都是连续的，

cues.en: I can't input exact values.
cues.zh: 我无法输入精确的值。

cues.en: So if I try to repeat the same calculation,
cues.zh: 所以如果我尝试重复同一个计算，

cues.en: I'm never going to get the exact same answer.
cues.zh: 我永远得不到完全相同的答案。

cues.en: Plus, think about manufacturing analog computers. There's always gonna be some variation in the exact value of components like resistors or capacitors.
cues.zh: 另外，想想制造模拟计算机。电阻器或电容器这类元件的精确值总会有一些偏差。

cues.en: So as a general rule of thumb, you can expect about a 1%
cues.zh: 所以一般来说，你可以预期大约 1%

cues.en: error.
cues.zh: 的误差。

cues.en: So when you think of analog computers, you can think powerful,
cues.zh: 所以提到模拟计算机，你会想到强大、

cues.en: fast, and energy efficient,
cues.zh: 快速、能效高，

cues.en: but also
cues.zh: 但也会想到

cues.en: single purpose, non repeatable, and inexact.
cues.zh: 单一用途、不可重复、不精确。

cues.en: And if those sound like deal breakers, it's because they probably are. I think these are the major reasons why analog computers fell out of favor as soon as digital computers became viable.
cues.zh: 如果这些听起来像致命缺陷，那很可能就是。我认为这些正是数字计算机一可行、模拟计算机就失宠的主要原因。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: here's why analog computers
cues.zh: 以下是模拟计算机

cues.en: may be making a comeback.
cues.zh: 可能正在回归的原因。

cues.en: It all starts with artificial intelligence.
cues.zh: 这一切都始于人工智能。

cues.en: A machine has been programmed to see and to move objects.
cues.zh: 一台机器被编程为能看见并移动物体。

cues.en: AI isn't new. The term was coined back in 1956.
cues.zh: AI 并不新鲜。这个词早在 1956 年就被提出。

cues.en: Cornell University psychologist Frank Rosenblatt built the Perceptron
cues.zh: 康奈尔大学心理学家 Frank Rosenblatt 构建了感知机

cues.en: designed to mimic how neurons fire in our brains.
cues.zh: 旨在模仿我们大脑中神经元的放电方式。

cues.en: So here's a basic model of how neurons in our brains work. An individual neuron can either fire or not. So its level of activation can be represented as a one or a zero.
cues.zh: 这是我们大脑中神经元工作方式的基本模型。单个神经元要么放电，要么不放电。因此它的激活水平可以用 1 或 0 表示。

cues.en: The input to one neuron is the output from a bunch of other neurons.
cues.zh: 一个神经元的输入是一堆其他神经元的输出。

cues.en: But the strength of these connections between neurons varies.
cues.zh: 但神经元之间这些连接的强度各不相同。

cues.en: So each one can be given a different weight.
cues.zh: 所以每个连接可以被赋予不同的权重。

cues.en: Some connections are excitatory,
cues.zh: 有些连接是兴奋性的，

cues.en: so they have positive weights, while others are inhibitory,
cues.zh: 所以它们有正权重，而另一些是抑制性的，

cues.en: so they have negative weights. And the way to figure out whether a particular neuron fires is to take the activation of each input neuron and multiply by its weight, and then add these all together. If their sum is greater than some number, called the bias, then the neuron fires. But if it's less than that, the neuron doesn't fire.
cues.zh: 所以它们有负权重。判断某个特定神经元是否放电的方法是，取每个输入神经元的激活值乘以它的权重，再把这些全部相加。如果它们的总和大于某个称为偏置的数，那么该神经元就放电。但如果小于这个数，神经元就不放电。

cues.en: As input, Rosenblatt's perceptron had 400 photocells arranged in a square grid to capture a 20 by 20 pixel image.
cues.zh: 作为输入，Rosenblatt 的感知机用 400 个排成方阵的光电管，来捕获 20x20 像素的图像。

cues.en: You can think of each pixel as an input neuron with its activation being the brightness of the pixel.
cues.zh: 你可以把每个像素看作一个输入神经元，它的激活值就是该像素的亮度。

cues.en: Although strictly speaking, the activation should be either zero or one, we can let it take any value between zero and one.
cues.zh: 虽然严格来说，激活值应该非 0 即 1，但我们也可以让它取 0 到 1 之间的任意值。

cues.en: All of these neurons are connected to a single output neuron,
cues.zh: 所有这些神经元都连接到一个单独的输出神经元上，

cues.en: each via its own adjustable weight.
cues.zh: 每个连接都有自己可调节的权重。

cues.en: So to see if the output neuron will fire, you multiply the activation of each neuron by its weight and add them together.
cues.zh: 要判断输出神经元是否会激活，需要把每个神经元的激活值乘以各自的权重，然后相加。

cues.en: This is essentially a vector dot product.
cues.zh: 这本质上就是一个向量点积。

cues.en: If the answer is larger than the bias, the neuron fires, and if not, it doesn't.
cues.zh: 如果计算结果大于偏置，神经元就会激活，反之则不激活。

cues.en: Now, the goal of the perceptron was to reliably distinguish between two images, like a rectangle and a circle. For example, the output neuron could always fire when presented with a circle, but never when presented with a rectangle.
cues.zh: 感知机的目标是稳定地区分两类图像，比如矩形和圆形。例如，面对圆形时输出神经元总会激活，而面对矩形时则绝不激活。

cues.en: To achieve this, the perceptron had to be trained, that is shown a series of different circles and rectangles,
cues.zh: 为了实现这一点，感知机必须接受训练，也就是向它展示一系列不同的圆形和矩形，

cues.en: and have its weights adjusted accordingly.
cues.zh: 并据此调整它的权重。

cues.en: We can visualize the weights as an image since there's a unique weight for each pixel of the image.
cues.zh: 我们可以把权重可视化为一张图像，因为画面的每个像素都对应一个独立的权重。

cues.en: Initially, Rosenblatt set all the weights to zero. If the perceptron's output is correct, for example, here it's shown a rectangle and the output neuron doesn't fire, no change is made to the weights.
cues.zh: 最初，Rosenblatt 把所有权重都设为零。如果感知机的输出是正确的，比如这里输入了一个矩形，而输出神经元没有激活，那就无需修改权重。

cues.en: But if it's wrong, then the weights are adjusted.
cues.zh: 但如果错了，权重就会被调整。

cues.en: The algorithm for updating the weights is remarkably simple.
cues.zh: 更新权重的算法非常简单。

cues.en: Here, the output neuron didn't fire when it was supposed to because it was shown a circle. So to modify the weights, you simply add the input activations
cues.zh: 这里，输出神经元在应该激活时却没有激活，因为它输入的是一个圆形。所以要修改权重，你只需将输入激活值

cues.en: to the weights.
cues.zh: 加到权重上。

cues.en: If the output neuron fires when it shouldn't, like here when shown a rectangle,
cues.zh: 如果输出神经元在不该激活时却激活了，比如这里输入的是一个矩形，

cues.en: well, then you subtract the input activations from the weights.
cues.zh: 那么，你就从权重中减去输入激活值。

cues.en: And you keep doing this until the perceptron correctly identifies all the training images.
cues.zh: 然后你不断重复这个过程，直到感知机能够正确识别所有的训练图像。

cues.en: It was shown that this algorithm will always converge so long as it's possible to map the two categories into distinct groups.
cues.zh: 事实证明，只要有可能将这两类数据划分为不同的群组，这个算法就总能收敛。

cues.en: The Perceptron was capable of distinguishing between different shapes like rectangles and triangles or between different letters. And according to Rosenblatt, it could even tell the difference between cats and dogs.
cues.zh: 感知机能够区分矩形和三角形等不同形状，或者区分不同的字母。据罗森布拉特所说，它甚至能分辨出猫和狗的区别。

cues.en: He said the machine was capable of what amounts to original thought
cues.zh: 他说这台机器具备了相当于原创思维的能力，

cues.en: and the media lapped it up. The New York Times called the Perceptron the embryo of an electronic computer that the Navy expects will be able to walk, talk, see, write, reproduce itself, and be conscious of its existence.
cues.zh: 而媒体对此大肆追捧。《纽约时报》称感知机是“电子计算机的雏形，海军预计它将能够行走、说话、看见、书写、自我复制，并意识到自身的存在”。

cues.en: After training on lots of examples, it's given new faces it has never seen and is able to successfully distinguish male from female. It
cues.zh: 在用大量样本进行训练后，给它从未见过的新面孔，它就能成功分辨出男女。它

cues.en: has learned.
cues.zh: 学会了。

cues.en: In reality, the perceptron was pretty limited in what it could do. It could not in fact tell apart dogs from cats.
cues.zh: 实际上，感知机的能力相当有限。它其实根本分不清狗和猫。

cues.en: This and other critiques were raised in a book by MIT giants Minsky and Papert in 1969
cues.zh: 1969年，MIT的两位巨擘Minsky和Papert在一本书中提出了这个批评以及其他类似质疑

cues.en: and that led to a bust period for artificial neural networks and AI in general. It's known as the first AI winter.
cues.zh: 这导致人工神经网络乃至整个人工智能领域进入了一段萧条期，被称为第一次AI寒冬。

cues.en: Rosenblatt
cues.zh: Rosenblatt

cues.en: did not survive this winter. He drowned while sailing in Chesapeake Bay on his 40 birthday.
cues.zh: 没能挺过这个寒冬。他在40岁生日那天于切萨皮克湾帆船时溺水身亡。

cues.en: The Navlab is a road worthy truck modified so that researchers or computers
cues.zh: Navlab是一辆经过改装的道路卡车，使研究人员或计算机

cues.en: can control the vehicle as occasion demands.
cues.zh: 能够根据需要在必要时控制车辆。

cues.en: In the nineteen eighties, there was an AI resurgence resurgence when researchers at Carnegie Mellon created one of the first self driving cars.
cues.zh: 20世纪80年代，AI迎来了一次复兴，当时卡内基梅隆大学的研究人员造出了最早的自动驾驶汽车之一。

cues.en: In The vehicle was steered by an artificial neural network called Alvin.
cues.zh: 这辆车由一个名为Alvin的人工神经网络操控方向。

cues.en: It was similar to the Perceptron except it had a hidden layer of artificial neurons between the input and output.
cues.zh: 它和感知机类似，只是在输入和输出之间多了一个人工神经元隐藏层。

cues.en: As input, Alvin received 30 by 32 pixel images of the road ahead.
cues.zh: 作为输入，Alvin接收前方道路30×32像素的图像。

cues.en: Here, I'm showing them as 60 by 64 pixels.
cues.zh: 这里我把它们显示为60×64像素。

cues.en: But each of these input neurons was connected via an adjustable weight to a hidden layer of four neurons.
cues.zh: 但每个输入神经元都通过一个可调权重连接到由四个神经元组成的隐藏层。

cues.en: These were each connected to 32 output neurons.
cues.zh: 这些神经元又各自连接到32个输出神经元。

cues.en: So to go from one layer of the network to the next, you perform a matrix multiplication.
cues.zh: 所以要从网络的一层过渡到下一层，你需要做一次矩阵乘法。

cues.en: The input activation times the weights.
cues.zh: 即输入激活值乘以权重。

cues.en: The output neuron with the greatest activation determines the steering angle.
cues.zh: 激活值最大的输出神经元决定转向角度。

cues.en: To train the neural net, a human drove the vehicle, providing the correct correct steering angle for a given input image. All the weights in the neural network were adjusted through the training so that Alvin's output better matched that of the human driver.
cues.zh: 为了训练这个神经网络，由人驾驶车辆，为给定输入图像提供正确的转向角度。训练过程中调整了神经网络中的所有权重，使Alvin的输出更好地匹配人类驾驶员的操作。

cues.en: The method for adjusting the weights is called back propagation, which I won't go into here, but Welch Labs has a great series on this, which I'll link to in the description.
cues.zh: 调整权重的这个方法叫做反向传播，我在这里就不展开了，不过 Welch Labs 有个很棒的系列视频，我会在简介里给出链接。

cues.en: Again, you can visualize the weights for the four hidden neurons as images.
cues.zh: 同样，你可以把这四个隐藏神经元的权重想象成图像。

cues.en: The weights are initially set to be random, but as training progresses, the computer learns to pick up on certain patterns.
cues.zh: 权重初始时是随机设定的，但随着训练的进行，计算机学会了捕捉某些模式。

cues.en: You can see the road markings emerge in the weights.
cues.zh: 你可以看到道路标记在权重中显现出来。

cues.en: Simultaneously,
cues.zh: 同时，

cues.en: the output steering angle coalesces
cues.zh: 输出的转向角逐渐合并

cues.en: onto the human steering angle.
cues.zh: 趋近于人类的转向角。

cues.en: The computer drove the vehicle at a top speed of around one or two kilometers per hour. It was limited by the speed at which the computer could perform matrix multiplication.
cues.zh: 这台计算机以每小时一到两公里的最高速度驾驶着汽车。它的速度受限于计算机执行矩阵乘法的速度。

cues.en: Despite these advances, artificial neural networks still struggled with seemingly simple tasks like telling apart cats and dogs.
cues.zh: 尽管取得了这些进展，人工神经网络在处理区分猫和狗这样看似简单的任务时仍然很吃力。

cues.en: And no one knew whether hardware or software was the weak link. I mean, did we have a good model of intelligence we just needed more computer power? Or did we have the wrong idea about how to make intelligent systems altogether?
cues.zh: 而且没人知道是硬件还是软件掉链子了。我是说，是我们拥有了一个很好的智能模型，只是需要更多算力？还是说我们对如何构建智能系统从根本上就想错了？

cues.en: So artificial intelligence experienced another lull in the nineteen nineties.
cues.zh: 因此，人工智能在二十世纪九十年代又经历了一次低谷。

cues.en: By the mid two thousands, most AI researchers were focused on improving algorithms,
cues.zh: 到两千年代中期，大多数 AI 研究人员都专注于改进算法，

cues.en: But one researcher, Fei Fei Li, thought maybe there was a different problem.
cues.zh: 但有一位研究员，李飞飞，认为也许是另一个问题。

cues.en: Maybe these artificial neural networks just needed more data to train on. So she planned to map out the entire world of objects.
cues.zh: 也许这些人工神经网络只是需要更多的数据来进行训练。于是她计划绘制出整个物体世界。

cues.en: From 2006 to 2009, she created ImageNet, a database of 1,200,000
cues.zh: 从 2006 年到 2009 年，她创建了 ImageNet，这是一个包含 120 万张

cues.en: human labeled images, which at the time was the largest labeled image dataset ever constructed.
cues.zh: 由人工标注的图像组成的数据库。当时，它是有史以来规模最大的标注图像数据集。

cues.en: And from 2010 to 2017, ImageNet ran an annual contest, the ImageNet large scale visual recognition challenge, where software programs competed to correctly detect and classify images.
cues.zh: 从 2010 年到 2017 年，ImageNet 每年都会举办一场比赛，名为 ImageNet 大规模视觉识别挑战赛，参赛软件要竞相正确检测和分类图像。

cues.en: Images were classified into a thousand different categories, including 90 different dog breeds. A neural network competing this competition would have an output layer of a thousand neurons,
cues.zh: 图像被分成一千个不同类别，其中包括 90 种不同的犬种。参加这项比赛的神经网络会有一个包含一千个神经元的输出层，

cues.en: each corresponding to a category of object that could appear in the image. If the image contains say a German Shepherd, then the output neuron corresponding to German Shepherd should have the highest activation.
cues.zh: 每个神经元对应一种可能出现在图像中的物体类别。比如，图像里有一只德国牧羊犬，那么对应德国牧羊犬的输出神经元就应该有最高的激活值。

cues.en: Unsurprisingly,
cues.zh: 不出所料，

cues.en: it turned out to be a tough challenge.
cues.zh: 这项挑战相当艰巨。

cues.en: One way to judge the performance of an AI is to see how often the five highest neuron activations do not include the correct category.
cues.zh: 评估 AI 性能的一种方法，是看激活值最高的五个神经元中，有多少次没有包含正确类别。

cues.en: This is the so called top five error rate. In 2010, the best performer had a top five error rate of 28.2%.
cues.zh: 这就是所谓的 Top-5 错误率。2010 年，表现最好的系统错误率为 28.2%。

cues.en: Meaning that nearly a third of the time, the correct answer was not among its top five guesses.
cues.zh: 也就是说，近三分之一的情况下，正确答案都不在它猜测的前五个类别里。

cues.en: the error rate of the best performer was 25.8%,
cues.zh: 表现最好的系统错误率为 25.8%，

cues.en: a substantial improvement.
cues.zh: 这是一次显著的进步。

cues.en: But the next year, an artificial neural network from the University of Toronto called AlexNet
cues.zh: 但到了第二年，多伦多大学的一个名为 AlexNet 的人工神经网络

cues.en: blew away the competition with a top five error rate of just 16.4%.
cues.zh: 以仅 16.4% 的 Top-5 错误率，远远甩开了其他参赛者。

cues.en: What set AlexNet apart was its size and depth. The network consisted of eight layers and in total 500,000
cues.zh: AlexNet的独特之处在于它的规模和深度。这个网络由八层组成，总共50万

cues.en: neurons.
cues.zh: 个神经元。

cues.en: To train AlexNet,
cues.zh: 为了训练AlexNet，

cues.en: 60,000,000 weights and biases had to be carefully adjusted using the training database.
cues.zh: 需要利用训练数据库仔细调整6000万个权重和偏置。

cues.en: Because of all the big matrix multiplications,
cues.zh: 由于大量的大型矩阵乘法运算，

cues.en: processing a single image required 700,000,000
cues.zh: 处理单张图像需要7亿

cues.en: individual math operations,
cues.zh: 次独立数学运算，

cues.en: so training was computationally intensive.
cues.zh: 因此训练在计算上非常密集。

cues.en: The team managed it by pioneering the use of GPUs,
cues.zh: 团队通过率先使用GPU来应对这一挑战，

cues.en: graphical processing units, which are traditionally used for driving displays,
cues.zh: 即图形处理单元，传统上用于驱动显示器、

cues.en: screens.
cues.zh: 屏幕。

cues.en: So they're specialized for fast parallel computations.
cues.zh: 所以它们专门针对快速并行计算进行了优化。

cues.en: The AlexNet paper describing their research is a blockbuster.
cues.zh: 描述他们研究的AlexNet论文是一篇重磅之作。

cues.en: It's now been cited over a 100,000
cues.zh: 它现在已被引用超过10万

cues.en: times and it identifies the scale of the neural network as key to its success.
cues.zh: 次，并指出神经网络的规模是其成功的关键。

cues.en: It takes a lot of computation to train and run the network, but the improvement in performance is worth it. With others following their lead, the top five error rate on the ImageNet competition plummeted in the years that followed down to 3.6%
cues.zh: 训练和运行网络需要大量计算，但性能的提升是值得的。随着其他人跟随他们的脚步，ImageNet竞赛的前五错误率在随后几年急剧下降，到2015年降至3.6%

cues.en: That is better than human performance.
cues.zh: 这比人类表现更好。

cues.en: The neural network that achieved this had a 100 layers of neurons. So the future is clear. We will see ever increasing demand for ever larger neural networks,
cues.zh: 实现这一点的神经网络有100层神经元。所以未来清晰可见。我们将看到对更大神经网络的需求不断增长，

cues.en: and this is a problem for several reasons. One is energy consumption.
cues.zh: 而这带来了几个问题。其中之一是能源消耗。

cues.en: Training a neural network requires an amount of electricity similar to the yearly consumption of three households.
cues.zh: 训练一个神经网络所需的电力相当于三户家庭的年消耗量。

cues.en: Another issue is the so called von Neumann bottleneck. Virtually every modern digital computer stores data in memory and then accesses it as needed over a bus. When performing the huge matrix multiplications required by deep neural networks, most of the time and energy goes into fetching those weight values rather than actually doing the computation.
cues.zh: 另一个问题是所谓的冯·诺依曼瓶颈。几乎所有现代数字计算机都把数据存在内存里，需要时再通过总线访问。在执行深度神经网络所需的大规模矩阵乘法时，大部分时间和能耗都花在取那些权重值上，而不是真正做计算。

cues.en: And finally, there are the limitations of Moore's law. For decades, the number of transistors on a chip has been doubling approximately every two years,
cues.zh: 最后，还有摩尔定律的局限。几十年来，芯片上的晶体管数量大约每两年翻一番，

cues.en: But now the size of a transistor is approaching the size of an atom. So there are some fundamental physical challenges
cues.zh: 但现在晶体管的尺寸已经接近原子大小。所以在进一步微型化方面，

cues.en: to further miniaturization.
cues.zh: 存在一些根本性的物理挑战。

cues.en: So this is the perfect storm for analog computers. Digital computers are reaching their limits. Meanwhile, neural networks are exploding in popularity and a lot of what they do boils down to a single task, matrix multiplication.
cues.zh: 所以这对模拟计算机来说是一场完美风暴。数字计算机正接近极限。与此同时，神经网络的人气正在爆发，而它们所做的很多事情归根结底就是一项任务：矩阵乘法。

cues.en: Best of all, neural networks don't need the precision of digital computers Whether the neural net is 96%
cues.zh: 最妙的是，神经网络不需要数字计算机那样的精度。无论神经网络是96%

cues.en: or 98% confident the image contains a chicken, it doesn't really matter. It's still a chicken. So slight variability in components or conditions
cues.zh: 还是98%确信图像里有一只鸡，其实都无所谓。它仍然是只鸡。所以元件或条件上的轻微差异

cues.en: can be tolerated.
cues.zh: 是可以容忍的。

cues.en: I went to an analog computing startup in Texas called Mythic AI.
cues.zh: 我去了一家位于德克萨斯的模拟计算初创公司，叫Mythic AI。

cues.en: Here, they're creating analog chips to run neural networks, and they demonstrated several AI algorithms for me.
cues.zh: 他们在这里制造用于运行神经网络的模拟芯片，并向我演示了几种AI算法。

cues.en: Oh, there you go. See, it's getting you.
cues.zh: 哦，来了。看，它注意到你了。

cues.en: Yeah. That's fascinating. The biggest use case is augmented in virtual reality. You know, if your friend is in a different... You know, they're at their house and you're at your house, can actually render each other in the virtual world. So it needs to really quickly capture
cues.zh: 是啊，太迷人了。最大的应用场景是增强虚拟现实。你知道，如果你的朋友在另一个……他们在自己家，你在自己家，实际上可以在虚拟世界里渲染出彼此。所以它需要非常快速地捕捉

cues.en: your pose and then render it in the VR world.
cues.zh: 你的姿态，然后在VR世界里渲染出来。

cues.en: So is this for the metaverse thing? This is very... Yeah. This is this is very metaverse,
cues.zh: 那这是为元宇宙做的吗？这非常……对。这是非常元宇宙的，

cues.en: very metaverse application. This is depth estimation from just a single webcam. It's just taking this scene and then it's doing like a heat map. So if it's bright, it means it's close.
cues.zh: 非常元宇宙的应用。这是仅用单个网络摄像头做深度估计。它就是取这个场景，然后做一个类似热力图的东西。所以如果亮，就表示距离近。

cues.en: If it's far away, makes it like black. Now all these algorithms can be run on digital computers, but here, the matrix multiplication is actually taking place in the analog domain.
cues.zh: 如果距离远，就变成黑色。现在所有这些算法都可以在数字计算机上运行，但在这里，矩阵乘法实际上是在模拟域中进行的。

cues.en: To make this possible, Mythic has repurposed digital flash storage cells.
cues.zh: 为了实现这一点，Mythic 改造了数字闪存存储单元。

cues.en: Normally, these are used as memory to store either a one or a zero.
cues.zh: 通常，这些被用作存储器，用来存储1或0。

cues.en: If you apply a large positive voltage to the control gate, electrons tunnel up through an insulating barrier and become trapped on the floating gate. Remove the voltage and the electrons can remain on the floating gate for decades, preventing the cell from conducting current. That's how you can store either a one or a zero. You can read out the stored value by applying a small voltage. If there are electrons on the floating gate, no current flows, so that's a zero. If there aren't electrons, then current does flow, and that's a one.
cues.zh: 如果你在控制栅极上施加一个大的正电压，电子就会穿过绝缘层向上隧穿，并被俘获在浮栅上。撤去电压后，电子可以在浮栅上保留几十年，阻止该单元导通电流。这就是你如何存储1或0的方式。你可以通过施加一个小电压来读出存储的值。如果浮栅上有电子，就没有电流流动，那就是0。如果没有电子，电流就会流动，那就是1。

cues.en: Now mythic's idea is to use these cells not as on off switches,
cues.zh: 现在 Mythic 的思路是，不把这些单元当作开关，

cues.en: but as variable resistors.
cues.zh: 而是把它们当作可变电阻。

cues.en: They do this by putting a specific number of electrons on each floating gate instead of all or nothing. The greater the number of electrons, the higher the resistance of the channel. When you later apply a small voltage, the current that flows is equal to v over r.
cues.zh: 具体做法是在每个浮栅上放入特定数量的电子，而不是只分全有或全无。电子越多，通道的电阻就越大。之后施加一个小电压，流过的电流就等于电压除以电阻。

cues.en: But you can also think of this as voltage times conductance,
cues.zh: 不过，也可以把它看作电压乘以电导，

cues.en: where conductance is just the reciprocal of resistance.
cues.zh: 电导就是电阻的倒数。

cues.en: So a single flash cell can be used to multiply two values together, voltage times conductance.
cues.zh: 这样，一个闪存单元就能用来计算两个值的乘积：电压乘以电导。

cues.en: So to use this to run an artificial neural network, where they first write all the weights to the flash cells as each cell's conductance.
cues.zh: 要用它来运行人工神经网络，他们会先把所有权重写入闪存单元，用每个单元的电导表示对应的权重。

cues.en: Then they input the activation values as the voltage on the cells,
cues.zh: 然后把激活值作为电压输入这些单元，

cues.en: and the resulting current is the product of voltage times conductance,
cues.zh: 产生的电流就是电压乘以电导，

cues.en: which is activation times weight.
cues.zh: 也就是激活值乘以权重。

cues.en: The cells are wired together in such a way that the current from each multiplication
cues.zh: 这些单元的连线方式会让每次乘法产生的电流

cues.en: adds together,
cues.zh: 相加，

cues.en: completing the matrix multiplication.
cues.zh: 从而完成矩阵乘法。

cues.en: So this is our our first product. This can do
cues.zh: 所以这是我们的第一款产品。它每秒能执行

cues.en: math operations per second.
cues.zh: 次数学运算。

cues.en: Yep. 25,000,000,000,000 math operations per second, and this little chip here burning about three watts of power. How does it compare to a digital chip? The the newer digital systems can do anywhere from 25 to a 100,000,000,000,000 operations per second, but they are big thousand dollar systems that are spitting out,
cues.zh: 没错，每秒 25,000,000,000,000 次数学运算，而这块小芯片的功耗大约只有 3 瓦。它和数字芯片相比怎么样？新一代数字系统每秒能执行 25 到 100,000,000,000,000 次运算，但它们是大型的千美元级系统，功耗高达

cues.en: you know, 50 to a 100 watts of power. Obviously,

isn't like an apples to apples comparison. Right? It's not apples to apples. I mean, you know, training those algorithms, need big hardware like this. You can just do all sorts of stuff on the GPU, but if you specifically are doing AI workloads and you wanna deploy them, you could use this instead. You can imagine them in security cameras,
cues.zh: 这不是完全对等的比较，对吧？确实不能直接比较。训练这些算法需要这样的强大硬件。你可以在 GPU 上做各种事情；但如果你专门处理 AI 工作负载，并且想把它们部署出去，就可以用这款芯片。你可以想象它用在安防摄像头上，

cues.en: autonomous systems,
cues.zh: 自主系统中，

cues.en: inspection equipment for manufacturing.
cues.zh: 以及制造业的检测设备中。

cues.en: You know, every time they make like a Frito Lay chip, they inspect it with a camera and the the bad Fritos get blown
cues.zh: 你知道，每次他们生产菲多利薯片时，都会用摄像头检查，不好的薯片会被吹

cues.en: off of the conveyor belt. But they're using artificial intelligence to spot which which Fritos are good and bad. Some have proposed using analog circuitry in smart home speakers solely to listen for the wake word like Alexa or Siri.
cues.zh: 下传送带。但他们用人工智能来识别哪些薯片好、哪些不好。有人提议在智能音箱中使用模拟电路，专门用来监听唤醒词，比如Alexa或Siri。

cues.en: They would use a lot less power and be able to quickly and reliably turn on the digital circuitry of the device,
cues.zh: 这样能耗会低很多，还能快速可靠地启动设备的数字电路，

cues.en: But you still have to deal with the challenges of analog. So for for one of the popular networks, there would be 50
cues.zh: 但你仍然要面对模拟电路的挑战。比如对于某个流行的网络，会有50

cues.en: sequences of matrix multiplies that you're doing. Now if you did that entirely in the analog domain, by the time it gets to the output, it's just so distorted that you don't have any result at all. So you convert it from the analog domain back to the digital domain,
cues.zh: 个矩阵乘法序列要做。如果完全在模拟域里做，到输出的时候信号已经失真得厉害，根本得不到结果。所以你要把它从模拟域转回数字域，

cues.en: send it to the next processing block, and then you convert it into the analog domain again. And that allows you to preserve the signal. You know, when Rosenblatt was first setting up his perceptron,
cues.zh: 送到下一个处理模块，然后再转回模拟域。这样就能保住信号。你知道，Rosenblatt最初搭建他的感知机时，

cues.en: he used a digital IBM computer.
cues.zh: 用的是数字IBM计算机。

cues.en: Finding it too slow,
cues.zh: 觉得太慢了，

cues.en: he built a custom analog computer complete with variable resistors and little motors to drive them. You know, ultimately,
cues.zh: 他就自己造了一台模拟计算机，配有可变电阻和小电机来驱动它们。你知道，最终，

cues.en: his idea of neural networks turned out to be right.
cues.zh: 他关于神经网络的想法被证明是对的。

cues.en: Maybe he was right about analog too.
cues.zh: 也许他关于模拟电路的想法也是对的。

cues.en: Now, I can't say whether analog computers will take off the way digital did last century,
cues.zh: 现在，我说不准模拟计算机会不会像上世纪数字计算机那样腾飞，

cues.en: but they do seem to be better suited to a lot of the tasks that we want computers to perform today.
cues.zh: 但它们似乎确实更适合我们今天想让计算机完成的很多任务。

cues.en: Which is a little bit funny because I always thought of digital as the optimal way of processing information.
cues.zh: 这其实挺有意思的，因为我一直认为数字化才是处理信息的最优解。

cues.en: You know, everything from music to pictures to video has all gone digital in the last fifty years.
cues.zh: 你看，在过去五十年里，从音乐、图片到视频，一切都实现了数字化。

cues.en: But maybe in a hundred years,
cues.zh: 但也许一百年后，

cues.en: we will look back on digital not as the endpoint of information technology,
cues.zh: 我们回头看数字化，会发现它并不是信息技术的终点，

cues.en: but as a starting point.
cues.zh: 而只是一个起点。

cues.en: Our brains are digital and that a neuron either fires or it doesn't,
cues.zh: 从神经元要么激发、要么不激发来看，我们的大脑确实是数字化的，

cues.en: but they're also analog
cues.zh: 但它同时又是模拟的，

cues.en: and that thinking takes place everywhere
cues.zh: 因为思考无处不在，

cues.en: all at once.
cues.zh: 且同时发生。

cues.en: So maybe what we need to achieve true artificial intelligence, machines machines that that think think like like us us,
cues.zh: 所以，想要实现真正的人工智能，创造出能、能像、像我们一样思考的机、机器，

cues.en: is is the the power power of of analog. Analog.
cues.zh: 或许需要的正、正是模、模拟的力量。模拟。
